stories.delivered_paragraph: Paramount Skydance has asked a federal judge to begin its antitrust trial over the proposed $111 billion Warner Bros. merger in November, while a coalition of 12 states and the Writers Guild of America want an April 5, 2027 start. The states say the deal would reduce competition in basic cable and theatrical distribution, while Paramount says it would strengthen competition with Netflix and Amazon; the timing matters because Paramount is due to pay Warner shareholders $7 million a day from Sept. 30 until closing.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Fender has demanded that rival guitar makers, including Yamaha and PRS, pull Stratocaster-shaped instruments from the European market after asserting newly acquired copyright protection for the iconic design. Some manufacturers have agreed to alter their models, while others are contesting the claim and calling Fender’s demands anti-competitive. The resulting litigation could determine whether one of the world’s most copied guitar body shapes can be controlled across a major market.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Researchers at Imperial College and Emlyon Business School say venture-backed startup founders face fraud pressures shaped partly by the incentives around rapid growth and fundraising. Their study tracked SEC and Justice Department civil and criminal securities-fraud cases involving tech founders from 2000 through 2023; a separate University of Toronto review identified 654 cases involving U.S. VC-backed startups. The research says fraud remains rare overall, but argues investors and startup culture can help normalize behavior that crosses legal lines.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Amazon, Alphabet and Tesla reported negative cash flow in their latest quarter as spending on AI infrastructure and other expansion projects climbed, while Meta’s cash generation fell 91%. Rising memory costs are adding to the strain just as major technology companies commit heavily to data centers and computing capacity. The figures highlight the trade-off investors are watching: AI may drive future growth, but the buildout is consuming cash well before returns are certain.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Paramount and state attorneys general have failed to agree on a start date for the antitrust trial challenging Paramount’s proposed Warner Bros. Discovery merger. stories.delivered_paragraph: Delaying a Social Security claim until age 70 increases a retiree’s monthly benefit, but it also locks in proportionally larger cost-of-living adjustments, MarketWatch notes. That detail matters alongside the broader debate over the program’s funding shortfall because higher initial payments compound over time. For people deciding when to claim, the trade-off is not simply between smaller early checks and larger later ones; inflation adjustments can widen the difference further.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Rescuers have recovered the remains of U.S. climber Mallory Geis after an avalanche struck a 10-person expedition on Pakistan’s Broad Peak, near the Chinese border. Authorities also identified victims from Oman and Nepal, while bad weather slowed searches and drones spotted additional people on the mountain; one climber remained unaccounted for. The recovery effort shows how quickly conditions on one of the world’s highest peaks can turn rescue operations into a prolonged search.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Hamas says it will disarm only after Israel fulfills earlier ceasefire commitments, pushing back on President Trump’s assertion that a U.S.-brokered Gaza agreement had produced a disarmament breakthrough. The group’s response makes clear that any pledge is conditional rather than an immediate, verified step. That gap leaves the central issue in negotiations unresolved: whether a ceasefire framework can produce concrete security concessions from both sides.

stories.delivered_paragraph: An estimated 60,000 people from Morocco crossed into Ceuta, the Spanish North African enclave of about 83,000 residents, in an unprecedented 24-hour surge, with dozens reported dead during attempts to reach it. Spanish officials said more than 48,000 had voluntarily returned to Morocco by Friday evening. The episode again exposes Ceuta’s vulnerability as a gateway to Europe and puts pressure on Spain and Morocco to explain what triggered the sudden movement.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A U.S. company’s medical-delivery drones are helping move supplies in Rwanda, offering a fast way to reach some communities. The limitation matters beyond Rwanda: drones can improve logistics, but reliable clinics, staffing and supply systems still determine whether patients can receive effective care.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Sony and Marvel’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” took in a record $72 million in domestic previews and was projected by industry sources to reach roughly $167 million to $173 million on its opening day, including previews. Estimates put its North American debut above $330 million, which would approach but not necessarily surpass “Avengers: Endgame’s” $357.1 million opening-weekend record. The launch gives theaters a potentially historic box-office boost and reinforces the drawing power of established superhero franchises.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The Toronto Tempo acquired forward Aneesah Morrow from the Connecticut Sun for the rights to Maria “Masha” Kliundikova and a 2028 second-round pick. stories.delivered_paragraph: Atlanta’s ONE Musicfest has canceled its 2026 event, pausing after 16 years to rethink and build what organizers call the festival’s next iteration. Founder Jason “J” Carter said the decision reflects a desire to innovate rather than reproduce the same format; the 2025 lineup included Future, Mary J. Blige, Ludacris and Jazmine Sullivan. The hiatus removes a major rap and R&B gathering from this year’s calendar but leaves organizers aiming to return with a redesigned event.

stories.delivered_paragraph: FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s disputed World Cup plans have prompted boycott threats from some countries, putting the 2027 Women’s World Cup at risk of becoming the first major tournament caught in the conflict. stories.delivered_paragraph: Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet added nearly $1.5 trillion in combined market value this week after reporting strong cloud growth and affirming or increasing AI capital-spending plans. Microsoft gained more than $600 billion, while Amazon and Alphabet each added over $400 billion; meanwhile, Meta lost about $85 billion and Apple more than $350 billion as investors questioned their AI spending or outlook. The split shows Wall Street is rewarding companies seen as converting AI investment into revenue while punishing those with cost-heavy, less certain payoffs.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Eaton reported record second-quarter revenue of $8.53 billion, up more than 21% from a year earlier and above the $8.13 billion analysts expected, while adjusted earnings per share reached $3.15 versus a $3.07 forecast. The power-management company also raised its sales outlook, partly because of a recent acquisition, and its shares rose after the release. The results offer evidence that demand for data-center power equipment remains resilient despite recent investor concerns about the AI hardware trade.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The S&P 500 ended July lower for the first time since 2014 after a volatile finish to the month, with the selloff led by chip stocks. Semiconductor shares posted their worst monthly performance in 24 years, according to MarketWatch. The reversal matters because chips have been central to the AI-driven market rally, so sustained weakness in the group would test investors’ confidence in the technology sector’s ability to keep carrying the broader market.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Index Ventures has raised $2 billion across three new funds, bringing its total available investing capital to $3.5 billion soon after its payout from Wiz. The raise gives the venture firm substantial capacity to back startups across stages despite a tougher financing environment for many young companies. Its ability to replenish capital after a major exit is a sign that established firms with realized returns can still attract money, even as investors remain selective about venture bets.
